{{short description|South Korean film director (born 1975)}} {{for|Jang Hun the Korean baseball player|Isao Harimoto}} {{family name hatnote|Jang||lang=Korean}} {{Infobox person | name = Jang Hoon | image = | caption = Jang in June 2017 | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|1975|05|04}} | birth_place = [[Jeongseon County|Jeongseon, Gangwon, South Korea]] | other_names = | education = [[Seoul National University]] - [[Bachelor of Design|B.Des.]] ([[Visual communication|Visual design]]) | occupation = [[Film director]], [[Screenwriter|writer]], [[Film editing|editor]] | years_active = 2005–present | module = {{Infobox Korean name/auto|child=yes|headercolor=transparent | hangul = %장훈 | hanja = 張薰 }} }} '''Jang Hoon''' ({{Korean|hangul=장훈}}; born May 4, 1975) is a [[Koreans|South Korean]] [[film director]]. He directed the films ''[[Rough Cut (2008 film)|Rough Cut]]'' (2008), ''[[Secret Reunion]]'' (2010), ''[[The Front Line (2011 film)|The Front Line]]'' (2011), and ''[[A Taxi Driver]] '' (2017). == Career == === 2005–2010: ''Rough Cut'' and ''Secret Reunion'' === Jang Hoon (along with [[Jang Cheol-soo]] and [[Juhn Jai-hong]]) worked as an [[assistant director]] under [[Kim Ki-duk]]. His debut film ''[[Rough Cut (2008 film)|Rough Cut]]'' (2008), about a gangster who wants to become an actor and an actor who thinks he is as tough as a gangster, was written and produced by Kim. ''Rough Cut'' was much more commercially oriented than Kim's own movies, and the star power of its two leading actors [[So Ji-sub]] and [[Kang Ji-hwan]] propelled the [[independent film|indie]] to more than one million admissions, resulting in a profit 10 times its low budget.{{cite web|title=The Rising Power of Chungmuro - Rookie Directors|url=http://world.kbs.co.kr/english/archive/culturenlife_realfield.htm?no=1286|work=[[KBS World]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130524013349/http://world.kbs.co.kr/english/archive/culturenlife_realfield.htm?no=1286|archive-date=2013-05-24 |date=22 October 2008}}{{cite web|title=CHANG Hun|url=http://koreanfilm.or.kr/jsp/films/index/peopleView.jsp?peopleCd=10060674|work=Korean Film Council|access-date=2012-12-18|archive-date=2012-05-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120526145753/http://www.koreanfilm.or.kr/jsp/films/index/peopleView.jsp?peopleCd=10060674|url-status=dead}} Jang's second feature, ''[[Secret Reunion]]'' (2010), benefited from the director's populist sensibility.{{cite web|last=Lee|first=Ji-hye|title=Director Jang Hun's Movie Picks|url=http://www.asiae.co.kr/news/view.htm?idxno=2010031514481043894|work=10Asia|access-date=2012-12-18|date=16 March 2010}} A story about two intelligence agents, one from South Korea and the other from the [[North Korea|North]] (played by [[Song Kang-ho]] and [[Kang Dong-won]], respectively), who approach each other in acts of espionage only to develop an unlikely friendship, the film sold 5.5 million tickets, making it the second highest grossing Korean film of that year. === 2011–present: Critical and commercial success === His third film, ''[[The Front Line (2011 film)|The Front Line]]'', was a large-scale war movie that came out during the 2011 summer blockbuster season.{{cite news|last=Park |first=Sung-hee |title=The Front Line spotlights the Forgotten War |url=https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/www/news/art/2011/06/135_89035.html |work=[[The Korea Times]] |access-date=2012-12-18 |date=16 June 2011 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121028093550/http://www.koreatimes.co.kr/www/news/art/2011/06/135_89035.html |archive-date=28 October 2012 }}{{cite web|last=Ki|first=Sun-min|title=Battlefield film begins at war's end|url=http://koreajoongangdaily.joinsmsn.com/news/article/article.aspx?aid=2939186|work=[[Korea JoongAng Daily]]|access-date=2012-12-18|date=22 July 2011|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130611034503/http://koreajoongangdaily.joinsmsn.com/news/article/article.aspx?aid=2939186|archive-date=11 June 2013}} Starring [[Go Soo]] and [[Shin Ha-kyun]], the film was the most well-received among the ample number of [[Korean War]]-themed films and [[Korean drama|TV dramas]] commemorating the 60th anniversary of the war. Through the guise of a mystery narrative, the film revolved around the story of South and North Korean soldiers carrying out meaningless sacrifices trying to capture a nameless hill.{{cite web|title=Director Jang Hun - The Front Line|url=http://www.asiancemagazine.com/2012/01/21/director-jang-hun-of-the-front-line--south-koreas-oscar-nominee|work=Asiance Magazine|access-date=2012-12-18|date=21 January 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120505004218/http://www.asiancemagazine.com/2012/01/21/director-jang-hun-of-the-front-line--south-koreas-oscar-nominee|archive-date=5 May 2012|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|last=Heskins|first=Andrew|title=On The Front Line: an interview with Jang Hun|url=http://www.easternkicks.com/features/the-front-line-jang-hun-interview|work=[[EasternKicks]]|access-date=2012-12-18|date=15 March 2012}}{{cite web|last=Conran|first=Pierce|title=Interview: 'The Front Line' Director Jang Hoon|url=http://www.modernkoreancinema.com/2012/03/interview-front-line-director-jang-hoon.html|work=Modern Korean Cinema|access-date=19 March 2012}} It was selected as [[List of South Korean submissions for the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film|South Korea's submission]] to the [[List of submissions to the 84th Academy Awards for Best Foreign Language Film|84th Academy Awards for Best Foreign Language Film]],{{cite web|last=Noh|first=Jean |url=http://www.screendaily.com/awards/academy-awards/south-korea-submits-the-front-line-for-oscar-race/5031143.article |title=South Korea submits The Front Line for Oscar race |date=2011-08-24|work=[[Screen International]]|access-date=2012-12-18}} but did not make the final shortlist.{{cite web|url=http://www.oscars.org/press/pressreleases/2012/20120118.html |title=9 Foreign Language Films Vie for Oscar |work=[[Academy Award|Oscars.org]] |access-date=2012-01-19 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120518164323/http://www.oscars.org/press/pressreleases/2012/20120118.html |archive-date=2012-05-18 }} Jang became the subject of controversy when former mentor Kim Ki-duk's [[documentary]]-style self-portrait ''[[Arirang (2011 film)|Arirang]]'' was released. In the [[Cannes Film Festival|Cannes]] [[2011 Cannes Film Festival#Un Certain Regard|award-winning]] film, the elder cineaste explicitly criticized him as "a betrayer" after Jang signed with the film production company [[Showbox]]/Mediaplex.{{cite web|last=Lee |first=Hyo-won |title=Cannes hears out filmmakers angst |url=https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/www/news/art/2011/05/141_87442.html |work=[[The Korea Times]] |access-date=2012-12-18 |date=22 May 2011 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130222060536/http://www.koreatimes.co.kr/www/news/art/2011/05/141_87442.html |archive-date=22 February 2013 }} Regarding the matter, Jang said, "I hope director Kim can find consolation through ''Arirang''. He is a great teacher and I still respect him very much. I feel very sorry as a pupil of his." In 2012 Jang, [[Kang Hyeong-cheol]] and [[E J-yong]] made [[short film]]s for [[Samsung Galaxy Note (original)|Samsung Galaxy Note]]'s ambitious [[Product placement|PPL]]-film project ''Cine Note'' starring [[Ha Jung-woo]].{{cite web|last=Lee|first=Claire|title=Smartphones help directors look at films from new angles|url=http://nwww.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=20120120000793|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130127071318/http://nwww.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=20120120000793|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 27, 2013|work=[[The Korea Herald]]|access-date=2012-12-18|date=20 January 2012}} Actor [[Ko Chang-seok]] has appeared in all four of Jang's feature films in supporting roles. In May 2025, Jang's upcoming film ''[[Canvas of Blood]]'' was one of the nine films granted by the [[Korean Film Council]] with financial support as part of their “Mid-Budget Korean Film Production Support” project.{{Cite web |author=신지원 |date=2025-05-26 |title=영진위, 중예산 한국영화 9편에 100억 원 지원 |url=https://www.ytn.co.kr/_ln/0106_202505261803442346 |access-date=2025-08-14 |website=YTN |language=ko}} In August 2025, actors [[Kim Nam-gil]] and [[Park Bo-gum]] were confirmed to star in the film.{{Cite web |last=김|first=진석 |title=[단독]박보검과 김남길… '몽유도원도' 드림 캐스팅(종합) |url=https://mydaily.co.kr/page/view/2025081418175600598 |access-date=2025-08-14 |website=마이데일리 |language=ko}} == Filmography == === Film === {| class="wikitable sortable plainrowheaders" ! rowspan="2" scope="col" |Year ! colspan="2" scope="col" |Title ! rowspan="2" scope="col" |Role ! rowspan="2" scope="col" class="unsortable" |Note ! rowspan="2" scope="col" class="unsortable" |{{abbr|Ref.|Reference(s)}} |- !English !Korean |- | 2001 | ''Hera Purple'' | 헤라 퍼플 | assistant director | | |- | rowspan="3" |2004 |''[[Samaritan Girl]]'' |사마리아 |assistant director | | |- |''[[Love, So Divine]]'' |신부수업 |assistant director | | |- |''[[3-Iron]]'' |빈집 |assistant director | | |- |2006 |''[[Time (2006 film)|Time]]'' |시간 |assistant director, assistant editor | | |- |2005 |''[[The Bow (film)|The Bow]]'' |활 |assistant director | | |- |2008 |''[[Rough Cut (2008 film)|Rough Cut]]'' |영화는 영화다 |director, script editor | | |- |2010 |''[[Secret Reunion]]'' |의형제 |director, script editor | | |- |2011 |''[[The Front Line (2011 film)|The Front Line]]'' |고지전 |director | | |- |2012 |''Cine Note'' 시네 노트 "Lost Number" | |co-director |[[short film]] | |- |2017 |''[[A Taxi Driver]]'' |택시 운전사 |director | | |- |TBA |''[[Canvas of Blood]]'' |몽유도원도 |director | | |} ==Accolades== === Awards and nominations === {| class="wikitable plainrowheaders sortable" !
